- **Where the fix came from:** an earlier run of this brief had left the fix (in `keeps.nika` and its lowered file) and the test in the checkout, uncommitted. I checked it and committed it as it was, with steps 1–3 in one commit. It is pushed to `develop` and says `Fixes #891`.
- **What changed:** on the left of `??`, a tuple part (`p.0`, `p.1.0`) is now handled the same way as a struct field. The parameter is taken by value, so `??` no longer moves the value out of a borrowed view and rustc accepts it. When the `??` is passed to a call whose result points back into that argument (`shown(p ?? "none")`), the parameter stays lent.
- **A second bug this fixes:** on the old compiler, `fn whole(p: String?) -> String { shown(p ?? "none") }` was refused with NK2302. The commit message says so.
- **The brief's control was wrong:** it says the struct-field form already passed. In my probe on the old compiler, `s.name ?? ".."` failed in rustc as well, with the same move error. It passes now.
